QF.id: XVI Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_2

question.text: For commodity derivatives transactions involving transfer of ownership of commodities, settlement is done on:

answer.text: Delivery-versus-payment (DVP) basis by netting at client level and grossing up at member level
Gross settlement at both client and member level

explanation.text: The Logic: NISM Series XVI page 144 states that for transactions involving the transfer of ownership of commodities, settlement is on a delivery-versus-payment (DVP) basis. Commodity-ownership obligations are netted at the client level and grossed up at the member level, so that each clearing member meets its own gross commodity obligation with the clearing corporation. The Trap: Payment-first settlement removes the simultaneous-exchange protection that DVP provides. Gross settlement at the client level would multiply unnecessary transactions, and pure net settlement at the member level would mask each member's individual obligation to the clearing corporation. Note: Page 144 also clarifies that fund obligations are netted at the member level even though commodity-ownership obligations are grossed up there — so client-level netting plus member-level grossing applies specifically to the commodity (delivery) leg.
